Q: Missed @AutoConfigureMockMvc in spring-boot-test-autoconfigure-4 (Spring Boot 4) A:

Due to the modularisation in Spring Boot 4, many classes have changed module and package.
@AutoConfigureMockMvc is now in the org.springframework.boot.webmvc.test.autoconfigure package of the spring-boot-webmvc-test module. If you review your test dependencies, as recommended in the migration guide, you will learn that you can add spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test as a companion to spring-boot-starter-webmvc. @AutoConfigureMockMvc will then be available once you've updated your code's imports.

pom.xml after migration: https://github.com/JavaOPs/bootjava/blob/boot4/pom.xml

Q: Confusion about the naming of binascii.hexlify A:

I think it's because english language, hexadecimal ends in l:

Clear -> clearify

hexadecimal -> hexadecimalify

Since hex is am abreviation we get this.

Q: How is the output from prompt responses formated in the tools? A:

No. Markup is a generic term that goes clear back to SGML, from which both XML and HTML derived, all 3 of which is "markup" in the name. The plain-text thing with stars and dashes is a specific notation called Markdown, which is not at all related to SGML.

Q: Onvif device manager crash A:

GetProfiles requires a token for the VideoSourceConfiguration, not only a SourceToken, see ONVIF operations: https://www.onvif.org/ver10/media/wsdl/media.wsdl#:~:text=GetProfiles

Q: Is there a way to implement smart rebase when using squash merge A:

I don't see how squash merge is relevant here. In the first graph main has a rewrite of commit A but not B. In the third graph it has a rewrite of both A and B and you're claiming there would be conflicts due to the squash merge. If you change the first graph to have main with ...A'---B'---F then you'll have the identical conflict as you would with the squash merge.
